name: Google SRE SLO Methodology Pack

sources.title: Google SRE Book - Service Level Objectives
Google SRE Workbook - Alerting on SLOs
Google SRE Workbook - Example Error Budget Policy

principles: An SLO is a target value or target range measured by an SLI.
SLIs should represent user-visible reliability wherever possible.
Availability SLOs should be based on good valid events divided by total valid events.
Latency SLOs should include a clear threshold, such as 95% of valid requests under 100 ms.
Error-rate SLOs should be expressed as failed valid events divided by total valid events, or equivalently as a success-rate objective.
SLOs should include a measurement window, commonly 28 or 30 days for monthly operational review.
Every SLO should have a defined error budget.
Error budgets should guide release and reliability trade-offs.
Burn-rate alerts should be used to detect fast and slow SLO budget consumption.
SLO rollout should include service-owner review, dashboard coverage, alert routing, and operational runbooks.
advisor_rules: Do not change deterministic SLO recommendations.
Do not invent telemetry or evidence.
Do not claim AI calculated objectives.
Use the deterministic SLOs as the source of truth.
Prioritize recommendations by user impact, confidence, alert context, and telemetry completeness.
Separate immediate rollout actions from service-owner review questions.
slo_review_checklist: Is the valid-event denominator clearly defined?
Does latency include a threshold in milliseconds or seconds?
Does the service owner accept the threshold as realistic and meaningful?
